q: Atoms consist of three sub-atomic particles called ____, neutron and electron.
e: Protons, neutrons, and electrons are the three fundamental sub-atomic particles that make up an atom.

q: A proton is a particle carrying a ____ charge.
e: Protons carry a positive (+1) relative charge.

q: A neutron is a particle carrying no charge and having a mass similar to ____.
e: Neutrons are neutral particles with a relative mass of 1, similar to a proton.

q: An electron is a particle carrying a negative charge and having a very small ____.
e: Electrons have a negative charge and a negligible mass compared to protons and neutrons.

q: The mass of an electron is approximately ____ times the mass of a proton.
e: The relative mass of an electron is about 1/1837 that of a proton.

q: In a neutral atom, the number of protons is equal to the number of ____.
e: Neutrality is maintained when the positive charges of protons balance the negative charges of electrons.

q: The proton number is referred to the number of protons in the atom and is often referred to as the ____ (Z) of the element.
e: The atomic number (Z) uniquely identifies an element based on its proton count.

q: The atom has a small, dense, positively charged center called ____.
e: The nucleus contains the protons and neutrons, holding most of the atom's mass.

q: The total number of these two particles is also known as the nucleon number or ____ (A).
e: The mass number (A) is the sum of protons and neutrons in the nucleus.

q: Outside and around the nucleus, electrons rapidly move in circular or near circular ____.
e: Electrons occupy specific paths or orbits around the central nucleus.

q: All atoms of the same element have the same number of ____.
e: The defining characteristic of an element is its fixed number of protons.

q: Some atoms of an element have different number of ____.
e: Variations in neutron count among atoms of the same element create isotopes.

q: These three different carbon atoms are called ____ of carbon.
e: Isotopes are variants of an element with the same proton count but different neutron counts.

q: Isotopes are atoms with the same number of protons but different number of ____.
e: This difference in neutrons results in different atomic masses for the isotopes.

q: Mass spectrometer is a device used to find out the masses of isotopes and their relative ____.
e: A mass spectrometer measures both the mass and the natural abundance of isotopes.

q: Isotopes of the same element have the same chemical properties but there are some small differences in ____ properties.
e: Chemical behavior is dictated by electrons, while physical properties like mass and boiling point can vary slightly.

q: A carbon-14 atom is ____ but carbon-12 and carbon-13 are not radioactive.
e: Carbon-14 is an unstable isotope that emits radiation, unlike the stable C-12 and C-13.

q: Some of the different elements have same ____.
e: Elements with different proton numbers but the same total nucleon number are called isobars.

q: Up to the early 20th century, uranium was used in making an attractive yellow ____ for pottery.
e: Uranium was historically used in ceramics before its radioactivity was fully understood.

q: Cobalt-60 (Co-60) is used in radiotherapy and in food ____.
e: Cobalt-60 emits radiation that can kill bacteria and extend the shelf life of food.

q: P-32 and Sr-90 are used to treat ____ cancer.
e: These specific radioisotopes are applied in the medical treatment of skin cancer.

q: Na-24 is used to detect tumors and blood clots and also detect the leakage from ____ pipes.
e: Sodium-24's radiation can be traced to find leaks in buried infrastructure.

q: I-131 is used to investigate the ____ glands.
e: Iodine-131 is absorbed by the thyroid, making it useful for diagnostic imaging and treatment.

q: C-14 is widely used in estimation of the age of ancient artifacts by ____ dating method.
e: Radiocarbon dating measures the decay of Carbon-14 to determine the age of organic materials.
